name: sol_basics_math_2
description: Precision loss/truncation in time-based arithmetic (e.g., rate-per-time calculations)
question: The source file in `source` performs a time-based calculation (such as deriving a rate, interest, or reward per unit time, or converting between time units) using integer division before multiplication or without adequate scaling/fixed-point precision, causing the result to truncate to zero or accumulate significant rounding error over repeated calls or long durations, and this is not merely an intentional, safe rounding-down that only ever favors the protocol/users in a negligible, non-exploitable way.
criteria: computes rewardRate = totalReward / duration then later multiplies rewardRate by elapsed time, truncating the fractional reward per second before scaling up
divides a timestamp difference by a large denominator (e.g., SECONDS_PER_YEAR) before multiplying by a principal or rate, losing precision due to premature integer division
calculates interest or fee per second by dividing an annual rate by seconds-in-year without any fixed-point scaling factor, causing the value to round to zero for short elapsed periods
converts a duration between units (e.g., seconds to days) using integer division and then uses that truncated value directly in downstream multiplicative calculations, compounding the rounding error
